explanation: Patent Rule 11 appeal; no pay-discrimination timing holding applied. Holmes cited on Federal Circuit jurisdiction; court expressly notes the AIA (the real override) and that it reaches only actions commenced after 16 Sep 2011; this action was filed April 2009.

Court borrows state limitations period under Graham County without mentioning Dodd-Frank, but the firing was September 2006 and the retaliation claim was filed March 2007, well before the 2010 amendment; limb 2 fails.

Buckhannon's prevailing-party test applied to a patent fee claim under 35 U.S.C. 285 and Rule 54(d), not FOIA; the OPEN Government Act left Buckhannon intact outside FOIA, so no superseded holding was applied.

Sutton cited only for the two regarded-as routes, not mitigating measures; footnote acknowledges the ADAAA and finds the facts (fall 2008 meeting) predate 1 Jan 2009, so pre-amendment law properly governs.

Florida oral-contract dispute; Eleventh Circuit Ledbetter cited solely for the judgment-as-a-matter-of-law review standard, not the pay-decision charge-timing rule; no Title VII pay claim, and events were in 2003.

Court applies Toyota's demanding standard and Sutton to disability, including a June 2009 accommodation claim, but expressly addresses the ADAAA and non-retroactivity in a footnote, and found a genuine dispute on disability anyway; limb 3 fails.

Rehabilitation Act claim on 2010-2011 employment; court applies Toyota's prevents-or-severely-restricts, permanent-or-long-term standard and pre-amendment cases to hold a temporary knee injury not a disability, never mentioning the ADAAA, which amended the incorporated definition.
